cases.sentence: — Mon cher Boris,[139] Милый дружок, — сказала мать, выпрастывая руку из-под ___ и робким и ласковым движением кладя ее на руку сына, — будь ласков, будь внимателен.
cases.explain: «старого салопа» — after the preposition «из-под», the genitive here marks possession, absence, or quantity.
cases.translation: “My dear Boris,” said Princess Anna Mikháylovna to her son as Countess Rostóva’s carriage in which they were seated drove over the straw covered street and turned into the wide courtyard of Count Kiríl Vladímirovich Bezúkhov’s house. “My dear Borís,” said the mother, drawing her hand from beneath her old mantle and laying it timidly and tenderly on her son’s arm, “be affectionate and attentive to him. Count Kiríl Vladímirovich is your godfather after all, and your future depends on him. Remember that, my dear, and be nice to him, as you so well know how to be.”

cases.sentence: Граф Кирилл Владимирович всё-таки тебе ___, и от него зависит твоя будущая судьба.
cases.explain: «крестный отец» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.

cases.sentence: — сказала мать ___, опять дотрогиваясь до руки сына, как будто это прикосновение могло успокоивать или возбуждать его.
cases.explain: «умоляющим голосом» — the instrumental marks the means, company, or complement.
cases.translation: “My dear!” exclaimed his mother imploringly, again laying her hand on his arm as if that touch might soothe or rouse him.

cases.explain: «петербургский доктор» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: Just as the mother and son, having reached the middle of the hall, were about to ask their way of an elderly footman who had sprung up as they entered, the bronze handle of one of the doors turned and Prince Vasíli came out—wearing a velvet coat with a single star on his breast, as was his custom when at home—taking leave of a good-looking, dark-haired man. This was the celebrated Petersburg doctor, Lorrain.

cases.sentence: — отвечал доктор, грассируя и произнося латинские слова ___.
cases.explain: «французским выговором» — the instrumental marks the means, company, or complement.
cases.translation: “Prince, humanum est errare,4 but …” replied the doctor, swallowing his r’s, and pronouncing the Latin words with a French accent. “Very well, very well …”

cases.sentence: — Да, в каких ___ пришлось нам видеться, князь...
cases.explain: «грустных обстоятельствах» — after the preposition «в», for location or topic.
cases.translation: “Ah, Prince! In what sad circumstances we meet again! And how is our dear invalid?” said she, as though unaware of the cold offensive look fixed on her.

cases.explain: «бесстрастным тоном» — the instrumental marks the means, company, or complement.
cases.translation: “Try to serve well and show yourself worthy,” added he, addressing Borís with severity. “I am glad. … Are you here on leave?” he went on in his usual tone of indifference.

cases.sentence: — Mais très brave homme, mon prince,[145] Но добрый человек, князь, — заметила Анна Михайловна, трогательно улыбаясь, как будто и она знала, что граф Ростов заслуживал такого мнения, но просила пожалеть ___.
cases.explain: «бедного старика» — the accusative marks the direct object of the verb.
cases.translation: “But a very kind man, Prince,” said Anna Mikháylovna with a pathetic smile, as though she too knew that Count Rostóv deserved this censure, but asked him not to be too hard on the poor old man. “What do the doctors say?” asked the princess after a pause, her worn face again expressing deep sorrow.

cases.explain: «последние минуты» — the accusative marks the direct object of the verb.
cases.translation: “If it were not for my sincere affection and devotion to Uncle,” said she, uttering the word with peculiar assurance and unconcern, “I know his character: noble, upright … but you see he has no one with him except the young princesses. … They are still young. …” She bent her head and continued in a whisper: “Has he performed his final duty, Prince? How priceless are those last moments! It can make things no worse, and it is absolutely necessary to prepare him if he is so ill. We women, Prince,” and she smiled tenderly, “always know how to say these things. I absolutely must see him, however painful it may be for me. I am used to suffering.”
